chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sahil from his father who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who had relations with his wife during the month of Ramadan while he was traveling, and he said, 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does marital intercourse invalidate the fast of a traveler in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that a traveler’s marital relations during the day of Ramadan do not invalidate their fast, distinguishing this ruling from that of a resident. This highlights the flexibility of Shariah for travelers, who are already exempt from fasting but retain the validity of their fast if they choose to keep it. The ruling underscores the principle that the penalty of *kaffarah* (expiation) applies specifically to residents who break their fast, whereas travelers are not subject to the same strictness regarding the validity of the fast itself.
